text:
Marcus Lin: Dropping a draft ADR outline for rotation + ciphertext backwards compat. Need sign-off on scope/contract before we lock implementation details. Draft: https://confluence.redwood.local/x/adr-0142-draft (WIP)

Marcus Lin: Core question: what EXACTLY are we promising wrt ciphertext encrypted under old key versions during scheduled rotation + emergency rotation. i.e. what’s “backwards compatible” mean in practice for Hosted/Dedicated/Private.

Ethan Park: thx. quick take: ADR should define (1) supported ciphertext formats/versions, (2) key selection rules (control plane), (3) decrypt behavior during rotation window (dual-read), and (4) failure/rollback semantics.

Ethan Park: also clarify what “ciphertext” refers to in our system (secrets blobs, stored connectors, cached artifacts?) vs anything customer stores themselves.

Benji Okafor: +1. for control plane config: we need deterministic key selection rules. current behavior risks “drift” if alias moves or provider rotates under us. ADR should explicitly say: encryption uses pinned key reference (provider key id + version when available). decrypt reads key reference from ciphertext header, not “whatever is current.”

Vikram Singh: from data-plane side, we should be careful about “decrypt forever” language. if customer disables or deletes a key, we can’t decrypt. contract should be conditioned on key material remaining accessible + policy allows decrypt.

Hanae Suzuki: esp in Private. customer-managed KMS means they own key lifecycle. we can provide tooling + checks, but we can’t guarantee they won’t disable old keys early.

Marcus Lin: yep. current ADR draft wording is: “Redwood guarantees continued decryptability of previously-encrypted artifacts across rotations, provided the prior key remains enabled and permissions remain intact.” too hand-wavy?

Jordan Lee: feels fine but we should spell out “permissions remain intact” = KMS `Decrypt` allowed for the Redwood service principal / workload identity in that env. Otherwise GRC will ask what control we have.

Olga Petrov: jumping in: we need a clean statement for customer/security reviews + evidence mapping. Suggest:
- Guaranteed behavior by Redwood software
- Assumptions / shared responsibility
- Explicit non-goals (e.g., retroactive re-encryption of all historical data by default)

Naomi Feldman: product lens: enterprise customers keep asking “will rotation cause downtime / data loss.” can we phrase it as: rotation is low/no downtime; old ciphertext remains readable; new ciphertext uses new key after cutover.

Diego Santos: also mention rollouts: we’ll stage it behind flags. ADR should define minimal contract so implementations in Hosted/Dedicated/Private don’t diverge.

Marcus Lin: ok, proposing we make the contract section very explicit:
1) Ciphertext format has a versioned header including `{provider, key_resource_id, key_version(optional), created_at, kek_ref}`.
2) Encrypt path uses “active key ref” from config (pinned), not aliases unless alias->id resolved at config-apply time and pinned.
3) Decrypt path attempts key ref from header; during rotation window can fall back to previous key ref(s) bounded.
4) Scheduled rotation: dual-read window default 7d (configurable), then old key can be removed from “fallback set” but NOT deleted/disabled by Redwood.
5) Emergency rotation: new key becomes active immediately; fallback behavior depends on incident severity but default still dual-read unless key is compromised.

Ethan Park: emergency rotation is where we need crisp language. if we ever disable old key, it breaks decrypt for old ciphertext. that’s incompatible with “no data loss.”

Marcus Lin: agreed. thinking: emergency rotation has 2 modes:
- “suspected exposure” (rotate now, keep old enabled, shorten dual-read)
- “confirmed compromise” (rotate now, and optionally disable old key to stop further abuse) => BUT we must acknowledge impact and provide mitigation (e.g., re-encrypt job if possible).

Vikram Singh: and be careful: disabling old key prevents decrypt even for legitimate workloads, not just encrypt. so service might go read-fail across any stored artifacts still under old key. we need a runbook path: keep old key enabled but lock down IAM to only decrypt from Redwood? not always possible if key is compromised.

Benji Okafor: from control plane: we can implement “deny encrypt under old key” by removing it from active config, but decrypt fallback still uses it. that covers most emergency rotations without disabling.

Hanae Suzuki: for Private, some customers use AWS KMS w automatic rotation on CMK. in that case key id stays the same; “version pinning” is different because AWS handles key material versions internally. ADR should note provider differences.

Ethan Park: +1. maybe ADR defines an abstract “key ref”:
- AWS: key ARN (no external version pin), optionally alias resolved -> ARN at apply time
- GCP: CryptoKeyVersion (versioned), can pin version
- Azure: key vault key + version
and we normalize in our schema.

Marcus Lin: yep, and ADR says: we never store “alias only” in ciphertext header; we store canonical key id/arn + version if applicable.

Olga Petrov: can we also add: audit evidence requirement: every key ref change (active key updated, fallback set changed) emits an audit event with who/what/when + change diff.

Marcus Lin: already in scope, but will add to ADR contract as non-negotiable. (ties into audit events spec + control mapping)

Connor O'Brien: release angle: I need to know what we’ll gate. If contract includes “dual-read window,” the feature flag should allow disabling fallback in canary if it causes perf issues. But ADR should define safe defaults.

Vikram Singh: perf: dual-read means extra KMS calls on decrypt failure. we should bound it: try new key first, then old key once. no multi-try across a list of N keys. Also cache negative results w short TTL so we don’t hot-loop KMS.

Ethan Park: makes sense. ADR should include a “bounded fallback” rule:
- decrypt attempt order: key in header (if header is authoritative) OR during transition, header may have “new key” while some data still old? (depends on re-encryption strategy)

Benji Okafor: I think header is authoritative per-object. dual-read window is only needed for:
- objects written during migration bugs
- objects where we changed header semantics
- and services that stored “key id = active” without persisting it (legacy)
So ADR should call out legacy ciphertext v0 that doesn’t carry full key ref, requiring fallback to config-defined set.

Marcus Lin: good catch. That’s the backwards compat part we need to lock:
- v0 ciphertext: includes only “key alias name” (older) or missing provider-specific id
- v1 ciphertext: includes canonical key ref
Contract: we will continue to decrypt v0 by consulting “legacy key map” in config, but new encryptions always write v1.

Jordan Lee: +1, and define how long we support v0. forever is scary; but dropping it is also scary.

Naomi Feldman: product: I’d rather not put “forever” in writing, but we can commit to “no breaking change without deprecation window + customer comms.”

Olga Petrov: for audits, “indefinite support” is not required, but we do need a documented deprecation process and notice period. Put that in ADR.

Ethan Park: so maybe:
- Redwood supports decrypt for all ciphertext versions we have ever produced, unless explicitly deprecated via security change process with >= 12 months notice for Private/enterprise (numbers TBD)
- plus: we won’t auto-delete/disable keys as part of scheduled rotation

Marcus Lin: ok, action: I’ll update ADR with:
1) explicit definition of ciphertext versions (v0/v1)
2) provider-specific key ref semantics
3) emergency rotation modes + what breaks decrypt
4) deprecation policy language (notice period, comms)

Marcus Lin: can I get quick sign-off on the “contract bullets” above as the ADR scope? 🙏

Ethan Park: scope ✅. I want one more line: “control plane must validate that active key + fallback keys are in same provider/region constraints for the deployment.” we’ve seen weird configs.

Hanae Suzuki: +1 esp in Private where region endpoints differ and IAM propagation delays cause false negatives. add “preflight checks required; failure is hard-block for apply/upgrade.”

Benji Okafor: scope ✅. Please include deterministic selection: “config apply resolves alias->id and persists resolved id; no runtime alias resolution in hot path.”

Vikram Singh: scope ✅ with perf bounds: max 2 decrypt attempts per operation (new then old), then fail. metrics emitted w key ref redacted/sanitized.

Olga Petrov: scope ✅. Add audit event requirements + evidence mapping stub. (I can help write the control language)

Connor O'Brien: scope ✅. once ADR updated, pls tag me so I can align rollout checklist + flags naming.

Marcus Lin: awesome. I’ll push ADR edits today and request formal approvals (Security + Platform + SRE) tomorrow. Will @mention folks on the Confluence page for sign-off.

Naomi Feldman: :thumbsup: pls also add a short “customer-facing summary” section at end. I can reuse for FAQ / sales.

Marcus Lin: will do.
